## Keywords

{{< glossary story-beat panel panel-caption thumbnail-sketch camera-move screen-direction >}}

## 10.1 From scene to beats

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A new beat starts when the place, the action, the speaker or the feeling changes.
- Each beat gets at least one panel.
- Two sentences with the same speaker and feeling stay in one panel.
- **Do it:** Mark the beats of the kitchen scene on your sheet. How many beats does it have?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/scene-beats.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · Beats

a) What changes when the scene moves to Salma's kitchen at night?
b) What changes when Nour says her first line?
c) Salma says two sentences with the same feeling. How many panels does she get?

::: {.answer}
a) a new place
b) a new speaker
c) one panel
:::

## 10.2 Draw it fast

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A panel is a thumbnail sketch that takes one or two minutes.
- Arrows show movement, and a dashed box with an arrow shows a zoom.
- The caption gives the shot size, the action or line, the sound and the time.
- **Do it:** Draw the five beats of the opening as five panels. Does each one have a caption?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/panel-anatomy.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Drawing panel 2

Panel 2 shows Nour jumping into the boat and rowing to the roof.
**What do you draw, and what does the caption say?**

::: {.reveal}
1. The frame, a water line, the boat, and Nour on the left third.
2. An arrow to the right, because she rows towards the roof.
3. Caption: "2 · Medium. Nour jumps into the boat and rows. SFX: splash, oars. 3 s."
:::

## Try it 2 · The parts of a panel

a) How do you show that Nour rows to the right?
b) How do you show a zoom to Salma's face?
c) What does a caption give besides the action and the line?

::: {.answer}
a) with an arrow in the panel
b) a dashed box and an arrow to it
c) the shot size, the sound and the time
:::

## 10.3 Check and time the board

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Every beat has a panel, and panel 1 shows the place.
- Feelings are close-ups, and the screen direction stays the same.
- The sum of the panel times is the length of the scene.
- **Do it:** Check your five panels with the checklist. How many seconds is your scene?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/board-check.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 3 · The checklist

a) Five panels have 2 s, 3 s, 3 s, 4 s and 2 s. How long is the scene?
b) A board starts with a close-up of Nour. What is missing?
c) Salma's fearful line is in a wide shot. What do you change?

::: {.answer}
a) 14 s
b) an establishing shot of the place
c) Make it a close-up.
:::

## Game challenge · Board Fixer

{{< sim file="sims/board-fixer.html" poster="sims/board-fixer.png" title="Board Fixer: find the problem in each storyboard" kind="game" task="**The story:** five storyboards of the Rooftop Rescue opening wait on the review table at Night Owl Games. **Play:** find what is wrong with each board, or say that it is ready." >}}

## Try it 4 · Fix and time (harder)

The facts: board 5 has a wide street (3 s), a medium Nour (3 s), a close-up of Nour (2 s), a medium Nour rowing (4 s) and a close-up of Salma (3 s).

a) How long is the scene?
b) The producer wants 12 s. Which panel goes first?
c) How many new panels does Salma's second sentence, “He's afraid of water”, need?

::: {.answer}
a) 15 s
b) the medium shot of Nour rowing (4 s)
c) none, because it goes in the same caption
:::

## Summary

- A new beat starts when the place, action, speaker or feeling changes.
- Each beat gets a panel, but not every sentence does.
- A panel is a fast thumbnail with a number, arrows and a caption.
- The checklist and the time line show when a board is ready.
